steps.observation: You have 60 seconds. Write a short story about a lighthouse keeper.

steps.action:
Every night, Old Thom climbed the iron stairs of Gull’s Point Lighthouse with the steadiness of the tide itself. He’d been doing it for fifty years—long enough, locals joked, that barnacles must cling to his boots.

At dusk, he polished the brass lens until it gleamed like a captured sun, then lit the lamp. From the gallery he watched the beam sweep across black water, stitching a path for wandering ships. Out there, captains trusted that steady pulse; in here, Thom trusted the music of gears and flame, a duet against the howl of wind.

One stormy night, the lamp sputtered. Lightning had cracked the oil line. Thom, heart hammering, dipped his kerchief into spare fuel, knotted it to an oar, and set it ablaze. He raised his makeshift torch through the shattered pane, rain needling his skin, until the machinery was repaired at dawn.

At sunrise, a freighter’s captain radioed in: “Saw your light, safe in harbor.”

Thom smiled. Somewhere between darkness and daybreak, he’d kept the promise he’d made half a century ago: no ship would ever miss the way home.
